full.description: This is a micrograph showing a section of gastrointestinal tissue, likely from the esophagus. The tissue exhibits signs of malignancy with infiltrating neoplastic cells visible within the stroma. Chronic inflammatory cells are also interspersed throughout the affected region. Based on these histopathological features, the appearance is consistent with metastatic carcinoma involving the esophagus.

blind.description: This image is a micrograph showing a tissue sample from the adrenal gland. The section reveals the presence of a metastatic carcinoma with the primary tumor originating in the stomach. The malignant cells infiltrate the adrenal tissue, disrupting the normal architecture of the endocrine system. The overall findings support a diagnosis of metastatic carcinoma involving the adrenal gland.

random.description: This is a microscopic histological image of kidney tissue stained with hematoxylin and eosin. The section shows pathological changes characteristic of nodular glomerulosclerosis, often associated with diabetic nephropathy, featuring mesangial expansion and Kimmelstiel-Wilson nodules. Interstitial changes and tubular alterations can also be observed throughout the renal parenchyma. The findings support a diagnosis of diabetic glomerulosclerosis.
